data.title: React
data.tagline: A JavaScript library for building interactive interfaces from components and state
data.learningOutcome: You can explain how a click changes a React value and refreshes the related interface.
data.description: After an item is added to a cart, React can update the count from 2 to 3. Whether the item was actually saved and remains after a refresh still depends on backend and data storage.

learning.assumes: You know a number on a button can change after a click.
learning.outcome: You can explain how a click changes a React value and refreshes the related interface.

explanation.title: A component is an interface piece that accepts inputs
explanation.text: Buttons and cards can be separate components. Components receive external parameters (Props, like title or price) to control content, allowing the same UI structure to be reused across pages.

explanation.title: State holds the current value
explanation.text: A click changes a counter from 0 to 1; state is what this part should show now.

explanation.title: React recalculates the view
explanation.text: React recalculates the related component and the renderer updates the needed DOM.

data.boundary: A component update is not a full-page reload. Requests, saved data, and URL changes are handled by other project code.

lessonPractice.title: Cart quantity appears in a product card, top badge, and checkout summary and must update together. How should it be organized?

options.label: Have multiple React components read one state and render together when quantity changes
options.feedback: One state becomes the view source, avoiding separate values and manual synchronization across locations.

options.label: Find three DOM nodes and manually rewrite each one's text after every click
options.feedback: Manual synchronization misses new locations easily and scatters the data source across operations.

options.label: Update React state and assume the cart remains after a page refresh
options.feedback: React updates the current view; persistence after refresh still requires local or server storage.

data.agentPrompt: Make the product card, top badge, and checkout summary read quantity from one cart state rather than editing DOM nodes. Update all three together, define persistence separately, and refresh to verify saved data.
